topic: Meaning, Scope and Development of Electronics
title: What Is Electronics? Explained Simply | PUC Electronics Class 11
description:
Aarav's phone fits in his pocket, yet it can do more than a 1946 computer that filled a whole room and used 17,468 vacuum tubes. What changed? Electronics. In this animated lesson we build the meaning of electronics from the ground up: the branch of science and engineering that controls the flow of electrons through a vacuum, a gas or a semiconductor.

On a live breadboard you see the difference between an electrical circuit (a switch and a bulb: on or off) and an electronic one (a tiny microphone signal controlling a big speaker current through a transistor), with the oscilloscope drawing the input and output waves as it happens. We derive n = It/e step by step, count the electrons a 2 A phone charger moves every second, and trace the development of electronics: Fleming's vacuum diode (1904), de Forest's triode (1906), the transistor (1947), Kilby's integrated circuit (1958), the first microprocessor (1971) and microcontrollers. Then the scope of electronics, the exam trap (electron flow vs conventional current), where it is asked, an original JEE Main pattern practice question with a full solution, and a formula card to screenshot.

This is Episode 1 of PUC Electronics, Class 11, Chapter 1: Introduction to Electronics (Karnataka PUC Electronics).
